input.correctedRule:
is_scheme_valid(s) is a pure, byte-wise, locale-INDEPENDENT function of the byte string s. No trimming, no case folding, no percent-decoding, no Unicode/multibyte awareness, and no length limit.

fn is_scheme_valid(s: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if s.is_empty() { return false; }                  // empty => false
    if !s[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() { return false; }   // 'A'..='Z' | 'a'..='z' only
    for &c in &s[1..] {
        let ok = c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'+' || c == b'-' || c == b'.';
        if !ok { return false; }
    }
    true
}

Equivalent anchored byte regex: ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*$

CHARACTER CLASSES (now exhaustive over every reachable byte 0x01-0xFF at both position classes):
- Position 0: valid only for the 52 bytes 0x41-0x5A and 0x61-0x7A. Invalid for every other byte in 0x01-0xFF, including all C0 controls 0x01-0x1F, space 0x20, all punctuation 0x21-0x40 / 0x5B-0x60 / 0x7B-0x7E, DEL 0x7F, and all 128 high bytes 0x80-0xFF.
- Positions >= 1: valid only for 0x30-0x39, 0x41-0x5A, 0x61-0x7A, '+' 0x2B, '-' 0x2D, '.' 0x2E. Invalid for every other byte in 0x01-0xFF, including ',' 0x2C (so the accept set is NOT the contiguous range 0x2B..0x2E), '_' 0x5F, '~' 0x7E, '%' 0x25, ':' 0x3A, '/' 0x2F, DEL 0x7F, all C0 controls, space, and all 128 high bytes 0x80-0xFF.
- CORRECTION to the prior rule's coverage claim: DEL (0x7F) is NOT unreachable via argv — only NUL (0x00) is. 0x7F was probed directly at position 0 and at positions 1..4 and is INVALID, matching the predicate. Behavior for an embedded 0x00 is genuinely unobservable through this driver (argv is NUL-terminated), so the predicate is unverified only for strings containing 0x00.
- Uniformity: identical rule at index 1, 2, 3, 4, at every index of a 10-char scheme, and at indices 1, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 511, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 50000, 100000 of long schemes. No "last character" exception (trailing '+', '-', '.' accepted). A single bad byte anywhere, at any depth up to index 100000, flips the result to false — the loop does not truncate or short-circuit early.

HIGH BYTES / LOCALE (verified, not inferred):
- All 128 high bytes 0x80-0xFF are invalid at position 0 and at every position >= 1. This is unaffected by locale.
- The scheme check is not locale-sensitive in any way. Tested under 20 locales (C, POSIX, C.UTF-8, en_US.utf8, en_US.iso88591, de_DE.iso88591, fr_FR.iso88591, tr_TR.utf8, tr_TR.iso88599, az_AZ.utf8, kk_KZ.utf8, lt_LT.utf8, lt_LT.iso885913, ru_RU.koi8r, el_GR.iso88597, he_IL.iso88598, ar_EG.iso88596, th_TH.tis620, ja_JP.eucjp, ko_KR.euckr, zh_CN.gb18030, zh_TW.big5, en_US@piglatin), each via three env mechanisms (LC_ALL only, LANG only, LANG+LC_CTYPE). Results byte-for-byte identical in all cases. In particular:
  * ISO-8859-1 letters (0xC0, 0xC4, 0xC9, 0xDF, 0xE0, 0xE9, 0xFF) stay invalid under Latin-1 locales -> no locale-aware isalpha/isalnum table is consulted, and no char-signedness leak into glibc's negative ctype indices is observable.
  * 0xAA (feminine ordinal, alphabetic in Latin-1) and 0xB5 (micro sign) stay invalid.
  * No Turkish-I bug: 'I', 'HTTP', 'IIII', and the full A-Z scheme remain VALID under tr_TR.utf8, tr_TR.iso88599, az_AZ.utf8, kk_KZ.utf8, lt_LT.utf8 — so no locale-aware tolower()/to_lower() is applied before an 'a'..'z' range test.
  * No multibyte awareness: under gb18030 / eucjp / big5 / euckr, a lead byte (0xB0, 0x8E, 0xA1, 0xC4) immediately followed by ':' does not get absorbed into a multibyte character; the "://" split and the per-byte class test are unchanged from C locale.
  * UTF-8 encodings of alphabetic characters are rejected byte-wise ("\xC3\xA9" -> invalid, both bytes fail).
- NBSP 0xA0, NEL 0x85, BOM "\xEF\xBB\xBF", and "\xFF\xFE" are NOT treated as whitespace: prefixing them to "http://host" yields an invalid scheme. Confirms no trim() and no high-byte whitespace class on this path.

NO PERCENT-DECODING: '%41://host', '%61%62://host', 'a%41://host', 'ht%74p://host', '%2Bab://host' all give LINE 2 = 0. Notably '%E9://host' is invalid — percent escapes are never decoded into (high) bytes before the check.

NO LENGTH LIMIT: all-'a' schemes of length 1000, 5000, 20000, 60000 are valid; all-high-byte schemes of length 100..100000 are invalid; no crash, exit code 0 in every case.

CASE: upper and lower ASCII letters equally accepted; no lowercase requirement and no lowercasing before the check.

REACHABILITY CAVEAT (what this binary can and cannot prove, via 'S://host' probes):
- Reachable and confirmed: schemes containing ':' or '/'. 'a:://host' -> scheme "a:" (LINE 2 = 0); 'a/://host' -> scheme "a/" (LINE 2 = 0); ':://host' and '/://host' -> LINE 2 = 0.
- NOT reachable: schemes containing '#' or '?'. parse() strips fragment then query from the whole input BEFORE locating "://", so 'a#b://host', 'ab?://host', 'http#s://host' all collapse to scheme "" with the remainder becoming a single path segment (e.g. 1|0|0|0|1|http). The predicate's verdict for schemes containing '#' or '?' is therefore an extrapolation, not an observation.
- NOT reachable: schemes containing 0x00.
- Only probes with LINE 3 = 1 and LINE 5 = 0 (host still parsed as "host") were used to read LINE 2.

INDEPENDENCE: high bytes elsewhere in the URL do not affect LINE 2 — 'http://h\xE9ost', 'http://host/\xE9', 'http://host?\xE9', 'http://host#\xE9', 'http://\xE9@host', 'http://host:\xE9' all give LINE 2 = 1. (Side observation, out of scope: a high byte in the host makes is_host_valid false — 'http://h\xE9ost' => 1|1|0|0|0.)
